title: The CSS Box Model
description: Understanding the CSS box model which includes content, padding, border, and margin.

flashcards.question: What are the four main parts of the CSS box model?
Which part of the box model contains the actual content?
What does padding do in the box model?
flashcards.answer: It creates space between the content and the border.

flashcards.question: How is the border in the box model defined?
flashcards.answer: It is the area surrounding the padding and content, visible as a line or edge.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of margin in the box model?
flashcards.answer: Margin creates space outside the border, separating the element from others.

flashcards.question: How does the box-sizing property affect the box model?
flashcards.answer: 'content-box' (default) sizes the box based on content only; 'border-box' includes padding and border in the total width and height.

flashcards.question: What is the default value of the box-sizing property?
If an element has width 200px, padding 10px, border 5px, and margin 20px, what is the total width including padding and border?
flashcards.answer: 230px (200 + 10*2 padding + 5*2 border). Margin is outside this.

flashcards.question: Can padding and margin accept negative values?
flashcards.answer: Padding cannot be negative; margin can be negative.
